## Part A — Creating Vectors and List:
```{r}
#Question 1:
#a.
worker_age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)
worker_age

#b.
length(worker_age)

#c.
min(worker_age)
max(worker_age)

#d.
worker_age[c(13:18, 33:35)]

#e.
worker_age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]

#f.
worker_age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
worker_age

#Question 2:
#a.
data(rivers)

length(rivers)
sum(rivers)
mean(rivers)
median(rivers)
var(rivers)
sd(rivers)
min(rivers)
max(rivers)

#b.
rivers_stats <- c(
  Length = length(rivers),
  Sum = sum(rivers),
  Mean = mean(rivers),
  Median = median(rivers),
  Variance = var(rivers),
  Standard_Deviation = sd(rivers),
  Minimum = min(rivers),
  Maximum = max(rivers)
)
rivers_stats

#Question #4:

vegetables <- list(
  "Carrot", "Cabbage", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Potato", "Eggplant", "Pumpkin", "Okra", "Radish", "Cauliflower"
)
vegetables

vegetables <- append(vegetables, list("Tomato", "Cucumber"))
vegetables

#b. How many data points do you have?
length(vegetables)

#c. Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5. What is the result?
vegetables <- append(
  vegetables,
  list("Lettuce", "Corn", "Bell Pepper", "Garlic"),
  after = 5
)
vegetables
#Answer: The four new vegetables are inserted after the fifth element. The list now contains 16 vegetables.

#d. How many data points does your vegetable list have?
length(vegetables)
```
